name: Iris Halpern
description: "Iris Halpern brings a record of fighting for working people and communities who have had their power and autonomy squashed. An attorney and former [Service Employees International Union (SEIU)](https://www.seiu.org/) organizer
column6: she has represented workers facing wage theft and discrimination. Her housing platform also recognizes that affordability and environmental justice are connected: it calls for more affordable homes
column8: and action on policies that drive displacement and pollution. This approach is directly in line with the Green New Deal’s promise to make people’s lives better while building a more healthy and equitable future."

name: Amanda Gonzalez
description: "Amanda Gonzalez is running to be Colorado’s next Secretary of State after serving as the Jefferson County clerk and recorder and leading [Common Cause Colorado](https://www.commoncause.org/colorado/). Her continued efforts focus on ensuring people can participate in democracy
column6: including voters with disabilities and people with past convictions
column7: and protecting Colorado’s accessible voting options. The Secretary of State’s office does not set climate related policy
column8: but ensuring our ability to vote and the legitamacy of the reported outcomes is more important now than ever. Amanda’s experience defending transparent
column9: accessible elections makes her an easy candidate to recommend to be responsible for protecting the value of our votes at the state level."

name: Lisa Escárcega
Race: State Board of Education Member - CD1
description: "Lisa Escárcega has spent her career working alongside students
column8: first as a school psychologist and then in education leadership. On the Colorado State Board of Education
column9: [she co-led the adoption of the state’s climate standards and progressive social studies standards](https://www.cpr.org/2022/11/10/colorado-state-board-of-education-approves-new-inclusive-social-studies-standards/)
column10: helping ensure students can learn about the challenges shaping their future. She has also worked to improve education funding and opposed efforts to privatize public schools. Sunrise and the Green New Deal view strong public schools and climate education as essential to a just transition: young people deserve the knowledge and resources to shape a livable future
column11: and every student deserves the opportunity to thrive."

name: Melissa Adriana Mejía
description: "Melissa Mejía has dedicated her career to advancing housing and economic justice
column6: focusing on policies that ensure equitable access to affordable housing and economic opportunities for marginalized communities. Her work emphasizes the intersection of housing
column9: advocating for solutions that address displacement
column11: and community empowerment. Melissa’s approach aligns with the Green New Deal’s vision of a just transition
column12: ensuring that all communities can thrive in a sustainable and equitable future."
